newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts' comments on ABN AMRO results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' comments on ABN AMRO results.

text.p: ABN AMRO Holding NV reported today that its 1996 net profit rose 26 percent to 3.30 billion guilders. The bank also announced plans for a four-for-one share split and an ADR listing on the New York Stock Exchange.
Below is some analyst comments on the results.

"The bottom line was in line with our estimates. The other news was no big surprise. Everybody had expected a share split sooner or later and the New York listing could have been expected too. Other Dutch companies are already listed there...The share split should help the share price and it supports our long-term buy recommendation.

"The four-for-one share split was bigger than foreseen. We had expected a split of about 2.5 for one. Investors usually like share splits even though they don't get anything more out of it...The ADR listing in the U.S. is also good for the stock. The results were in line with expectations but the 0.60 guilder rise in the dividend will give the market confidence. The worst thing I can say about ABN AMRO is that it is excellent. Over the next 18 months I expect it to be involved in some big acquisitions in European financial markets..."

"The bottom line figure is very good. We expected a stock split, but we thought it would be a two-for-one. One positive surprise is that only half of the old (hidden) VAR reserve will go into the new (open) FAR reserve which is less than I expected. In future, allocations to the FAR will be relatively low. This will have a positive impact on earnings per share."
"Overall, we are positive about the bank's 1996 results and about its 1997 prospects. The stock split and the New York listing will increase liquidity of the shares.

"The VAR is about the size we expected, but we had expected the allocation to the equity base to be minor. The substantial strengthening of the bank's equity base is extremely positive. It gives the bank a healthy base for further expansion.

"It also shows the bank is confident about the quality of its loan portfolio. Over the coming years, this will contribute to a higher EPS as allocations to the fund for general banking risks will be comparatively low.
"Given current uncertainties over the economy and the markets, I don't consider the absence of a 1997 forecast as a problem."
"The profit and hidden reserves were in line with expectations. A share split always works, investors like that although it's only a psychological thing.

"The U.S. listing is very good for the stock as it means it will be more international and will open doors for U.S. pension funds to invest in ABN as they are not obliged to invest in a stock that has no U.S. listing.
"ABN should be able to show an average increase in profits of 12-15 percent in the years to come. Another current positive is the dollar rate."
